description:
The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is a crop insurance scheme launched by the Government of India. 

It was introduced in 2016 to provide financial support to farmers in case of crop failure due to natural calamities. 

The main objective is to stabilize the income of farmers and encourage them to adopt modern agricultural practices. 

The scheme covers various risks including crop loss due to droughts floods and pests. 

Farmers receive compensation based on the area and type of crop insured. 

The benefits include premium subsidies for farmers which reduce their financial burden. 

Farmers can avail of insurance coverage for Kharif Rabi and other seasonal crops. 

The eligibility criteria include being a farmer who cultivates notified crops in the notified area. 

Farmers must also have a bank account and must be registered under the scheme. 

The application process involves filling out the prescribed form and submitting it to the local agriculture office or online through the official portal. 

The timeline for applying is generally before the sowing season of the respective crops. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare in collaboration with various state governments. 

Insurance companies are also involved in the implementation of the scheme. 

The scheme aims to provide timely compensation to farmers to help them recover from losses. 

It promotes the use of technology in assessing crop damage and processing claims. 

The scheme is part of the larger initiative to enhance the agricultural sector in India.
